summary: HTTPConnection is the leaf connection for HTTP/HTTPS: connect() creates an httpx.Client from the emitted connect kwargs (base_url, headers, auth, timeouts) and disconnect() closes it. Client construction failures are mapped to ConnectionTimeoutError or TransportConnectionError. It is also the fallback leaf for unknown provider types.
key_classes: HTTPConnection — ConnectionProtocol leaf owning one httpx.Client
key_functions: HTTPConnection(connect_kwargs: dict) — store kwargs; no I/O
HTTPConnection.connect() -> Self — release any previous client, then build httpx.Client(**kwargs)
HTTPConnection.disconnect() -> None — idempotent close; raises TransportConnectionError if close fails
extension_points: Behaviour is driven entirely by connect_kwargs emitted by the profile and auth profile (TargetFamily.HTTP)
lifecycle_notes: connect() is re-entrant: it disconnects the previous client before replacing it.
__enter__ returns self without connecting; __exit__ disconnects and attaches cleanup failures as notes when the body raised.
Imports httpx at module import; available only with the [http] extra.
The HTTP storage backend wraps the client in HttpRequestEngine; the engine borrows it and this connection owns it.
documentation_hooks: Connections reference: HTTPConnection lifecycle and kwargs
HTTP stack layering: HTTPConnection → HttpRequestEngine → HTTPStorageBackend
risks: Because create_connection defaults unknown providers to HTTPConnection, this class can be instantiated with non-HTTP kwargs and fail late at httpx.Client(**kwargs) with a generic TransportConnectionError.
Constructing httpx.Client performs no network I/O, so the timeout/connect-error branches in connect() are largely defensive.
